cards.title: Introduction to Logging in Flask
cards.content: Logging is crucial for monitoring application health, debugging errors, and tracking user activity in Flask. Python's built-in logging module is seamlessly integrated into Flask via app.logger.

cards.title: Understanding Log Levels
cards.content:
Logging levels indicate the severity of an event. In Python and Flask, standard levels in increasing order of severity are:

  • DEBUG: Detailed information for diagnosing problems.
  • INFO: Confirmation that things are working as expected.
  • WARNING: Indication that something unexpected happened or a problem might occur soon.
  • ERROR: A more serious problem preventing the software from performing a function.
  • CRITICAL: A severe error indicating the program itself may be unable to continue running.

cards.title: Configuring Handlers and Formatters
cards.content:
By default, Flask logs to the standard error stream. You can configure handlers to write logs to files, rotation files, or external services.

import logging
from logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler

if not app.debug:
    file_handler = RotatingFileHandler('logs/flaskapp.log', maxBytes=10240, backupCount=10)
    file_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    app.logger.addHandler(file_handler)
